_format.about: What /corp-jev has absorbed from outside itself, so it can be kept current. One row per source in `sources`; add a row the day /corp-jev absorbs something new, and bump last_absorbed when a `/corp-jev refresh` re-reads a source and folds in what changed.
_format.last_absorbed: YYYY-MM-DD: the day /corp-jev last re-read it and folded in what changed
_format.what: one line: what /corp-jev took from it
_format.refresh_days: re-read cadence in days (a positive integer); a row is DUE once the days since last_absorbed exceed refresh_days
_format.reader: scripts/preflight.sh prints [fresh] lines from this file (count, oldest row, due rows) and turns due rows into a note suggesting `/corp-jev refresh`; it is informational and never PARKs

sources.what: Entry point to TypeSafe's live docs (primitives, state, confidence, API, cookbooks): the source of truth for how /corp-jev words Jev questions.

Question design: one narrow judgment per question, a no-match option, independent questions batched over one state, named JSON fields in state (for new or unmeasured questions; a measured question keeps the plain-text rows it was measured on).

`jev verify` and corp-kit cascadeRoute/CASCADE_CRITERIA: supported/unsupported/declined with the relevance clause, send at confidence >= 0.8, missing confidence = 0, declined hands off to a human. /corp-jev departs from it where its human is the owner: a double failure goes to the front of the claim audit, not to them.

`jev gate` and corp-kit gateDecision/GATE_DECISION: deterministic checks first, named yes-checks over one state in one request, approve >= 0.9 / block <= 0.1 / else review. /corp-jev's checks are the registry's go_act entry, over the E0 row the owner's GO adopted.
Index to OpenRouter's Jev cookbooks and the /api/v1/systemone and /api/alpha/decisions references (a state may be a string, an object or an array).
Current Claude model IDs, aliases and tiers behind the section MODEL seat map.
How the harness resolves the `sonnet`/`opus` aliases, and the version floors preflight's [model] check reads (Sonnet 5.5 >= 2.1.284, Opus 5.5 >= 2.1.280).
Community Jev kit for Claude Code (a code pre-filter ahead of Jev on tool calls, plus triage, review and browse tools): practitioner patterns read in the 09-28 research lane.
Reference Jev browser agent: code builds the options from the live page, Jev picks one, code executes it; instructions sent as named fields.
Batching: items keyed or embedded (0 of 320 wrong) versus positional references (86 of 320 wrong at 150 items); since wave 2 (09-28) /corp-jev sends each row as its own state (packing v2).

Skill lifecycle: after an auto-compaction Claude Code re-attaches only the first 5,000 tokens of each invoked skill (25,000 combined) — why both cores stay at or under 12,000 bytes (preflight fails loudly past it) and re-invoke after a compaction.
Workflow runtime contracts in references/harness.md: concurrency and item limits, null slots in pipeline(), resume prefix replay, cache sharing and TTL, the Large-workflow warning.

Agent definitions in ~/.claude/agents/ behind references/model.md Law 2 (CEO decision E11): a definition's `effort` "Overrides the session effort level" and the Agent tool has no effort field, so Agent-tool seats use the corp-* types; a per-invocation `model` overrides the definition's; /tasks shows each subagent's model and effort (>= 2.1.242); a session started before ~/.claude/agents/ existed needs a restart to see new types. (A raw copy of the page is not included in this repo.)
Effort levels and per-model defaults behind references/model.md's effort-per-role table.

Sonnet 5.5 behaviour /corp-jev relies on: it may stop to check in at low/medium on long agentic work (the kit's unattended clause) and answers structured tasks without thinking unless told (the audits' think-first line).
Skill authoring rules applied in the 09-28 rewrite: references one level deep, contents lists on long references, third-person descriptions, no time-conditional rules.

Vendor numbers in references/model.md (Sonnet 5.5: FrontierCode 52.1% at xhigh, 46.2% at max; GDPval-AA 1844; price) and Law 3's reading of them: parity only at the top of its effort range ("At higher settings, it can perform comparably at a similar cost"; "Opus 5.5 remains clearly stronger at complex, open-ended work requiring sustained judgment") — why document builders run opus xhigh.
Vendor numbers in references/model.md (Opus 5.5 vs Fable 5.1; price; results at max effort unless noted).
§GATE: the static list of deterministic checks, not the threshold, is the security boundary; unknown answers never approve.
Clause 2.3(b): Jev output is never used to train or distill a model; ~/.cache/jev/judgments.jsonl is for threshold tuning only.
Facts first, then Jev: a done-check that computes transcript facts before asking Jev (AUROC 0.976 vs 0.777 on wording alone); pattern 68 and the hooks' hardening.
RELAYED and STALE rules in references/evidence.md (a figure only a subagent reported is re-read at source; self-changing outside state is re-checked).

Haiku 5.5: $0.10/$0.50 per MTok (prompts <= 100k), all five effort levels (default medium), vendor benchmarks at max; Claude Code haiku alias -> Haiku 5.5 from 2.1.293 on the Anthropic API (model-config). Absorbed as model.md H1 (corp-mech on haiku/medium after a measured tie).
